growth_signal.value: Reports reaching over 380 million users through brands like Britannia, Netflix, AJIO, and WPP, and has drawn new backing interest from QED Investors and Shah Rukh Khan.

entry.idea: Brands want interactive, augmented-reality style content for ads and packaging but don't want to build the technology themselves, so Flam gives them a platform to create and publish it.
entry.lesson: Package a hard technology, here mixed reality, as an easy tool non-technical marketing teams can use, then scale it across many brands at once.
entry.name: Flam

growth.basis: number: self-reported user reach, supported by new investor interest
growth.reason: The 380-million-user figure is self-reported with no independent numbers to confirm it, but new investor interest from QED Investors and Shah Rukh Khan backs up the growth story.

market.reason: Brand marketing and advertising is a large, worldwide industry, and interactive content is relevant to nearly any consumer brand.

tech.reason: Building a reliable mixed-reality content platform that scales across big brands is solid engineering, though a well-funded team could build something similar within a year or two.

sources.title: Flam Bags $4.5 Mn To Help Brands Create Mixed Reality Content
Govt to match VC investments in chip startups; Shah Rukh Khan, QED Investors back Flam

entry.twist: Its content already runs at huge scale, reportedly reaching over 380 million users through brands like Britannia, Netflix, AJIO, and WPP.
entry.who_pays: Brands and marketing agencies who pay Flam to create and run these interactive campaigns.
entry.why_now: Phones are now powerful enough to run rich augmented and mixed-reality experiences at scale, so brands can add this to everyday marketing instead of it being a novelty.
